neighbours.label: wild animals' seasonal movement and breeding cycle, especially fish and whales: salmon runs, spawning grounds, staging areas, migration; the + pole is the other side of the same animals, fish as food (fillet, seafood, fishmeal)
fire: Each autumn the sockeye return to their spawning grounds in the upper river.
Gray whales pass this headland twice a year on their long migration to the lagoons.
Thousands of sandpipers rest at staging sites on the mudflats before flying north.
The new culvert would block steelhead runs that spawn in the creek.
Herring gather in the bay every March to spawn among the eelgrass.
Satellite tags revealed the migration routes of young sea turtles across the gulf.
The weir was removed so that chinook could reach their spawning habitat again.
Caribou herds cross the river on their spring migration to the calving grounds.
quiet: Each autumn the cooks smoke sockeye over alder chips in the upper village.
Gray seals lie on this headland all day and bark at passing boats.
Thousands of sandpipers were painted on the mural beside the old harbour office.
The new menu would feature steelhead baked with lemon and dill.
Herring are pickled in the town every March and sold at the fair.
Close-up photographs revealed the shell patterns of young sea turtles in the aquarium.
The grill was cleaned so that the chinook steaks would not stick again.
Caribou stew simmers on the stove while the hunters mend their snowshoes.

notes: Card: ' spawning' x4, ' grounds' x3, ' staging' x2, ' migration' x2. Probes: salmon runs 0.96, whale migration 0.73, bird staging/migration 0.52; salmon fillet 0.07, lions resting 0.03. Near misses keep the animals and drop the migration/spawning sense.
